**The Weight of Unwritten Words**

There’s a quiet terror in the blank page, isn’t there? Not the kind that makes your hands shake or your breath hitch, but something deeper—a slow, creeping dread that settles in your bones like winter fog. It’s not the fear of failure, exactly, though that’s part of it. It’s the fear of *emptiness*. The terror of realizing that no matter how many words you spill onto the page, they’ll never quite capture the shape of what you’re trying to say.

I’ve been staring at this screen for what feels like hours, and yet the cursor blinks at me like a judgmental eye. *Go on. Say something.* But what? The words feel heavy in my throat, like stones I’ve swallowed by accident. Maybe it’s because I’ve spent so long trying to make sense of things—of life, of love, of the way time slips through your fingers like sand—only to realize that sense is just another word we’ve invented to pretend we’re in control.

Or maybe it’s simpler than that. Maybe I’m just tired.

Tired of the noise. Tired of the constant hum of the world, the way it demands you *do* something, *be* something, *mean* something. Tired of the pressure to turn every thought into a tweet, every feeling into a post, every moment into content. We’ve become so afraid of silence that we’d rather fill it with noise than listen to what’s underneath.

But silence isn’t empty. It’s full. Full of the hum of the universe, the whisper of your own breath, the echo of all the things you’ve never said. Silence is where the real words live—the ones that don’t need to be polished or performative or *liked*. The ones that just *are*.

So maybe that’s what I’ll do. Not write a grand manifesto or a profound reflection or even a coherent thought. Maybe I’ll just sit here in the quiet and let the words come out however they want. Messy. Unfiltered. Real.

Because the page isn’t the problem. The problem is the expectation that what we write should mean something. That it should *matter*. But what if it doesn’t? What if the only thing that matters is that we *tried*? That we showed up, even when it felt pointless? That we let the words fall where they may, without apology or explanation?

I don’t know. Maybe that’s the point. Maybe the beauty of writing—of living—isn’t in the destination, but in the stumbling. In the half-formed sentences. In the moments where you realize you’ve been writing the wrong thing all along, and that’s okay.

So here’s to the unwritten words. To the ones that get lost in the shuffle. To the ones that never make it past the first draft. To the ones that only you will ever read. They matter too.

Even if no one else ever knows they existed.

Even if they don’t make sense.

Even if they’re just… words.

That’s enough.
